# A Cosmic Question Mark

A streak of light flashed across the sky above France in April—but was it debris from the distant comet glowing nearby, or something else entirely? Scientists face this detective puzzle constantly: while comets do seed Earth's atmosphere with dusty debris that ignites as meteors, thousands of icy visitors orbit our inner solar system, making it nearly impossible to match individual shooting stars to their cosmic parents. November brings three chances to spot meteors from known sources—the Southern and Northern Taurids (both born from Comet Encke) in the coming weeks, followed by the spectacular Leonids meteor shower mid-month, which traces back to Comet Tempel-Tuttle.
